N.q: What does laser surgery use to make precise cuts and remove tissue?
N.explain: Laser surgery uses an intense beam of light to make precise cuts and remove tissue.

N.q: Which of the following sentences does NOT describe a laser?
N.explain: Lasers are high-intensity beams of light, not low intensity.
options: It keeps the tissue surrounding the tumor intact
It only cures specific types of cancer
It can be manipulated to create precise incisions

N.q: Compared to traditional surgery, what is true about laser surgery?
N.explain: Laser surgery targets tumor cells more precisely than traditional surgery.
options: It targets tumor cells more precisely
It takes a longer time but causes less bleeding
There is more damage to normal tissue
The risk of infection is high

N.q: In the context of laser surgery, what does the word 'manipulated' mean?
N.explain: 'Manipulated' means controlled or handled skillfully.

N.q: What is an endoscope?
N.explain: An endoscope is a flexible tube that helps explore internal organs.
options: A rigid tube inserted into the body
A flexible tube that helps explore internal organs
A tool suitable for cancers on the skin surface
An instrument used along with a scalpel

N.q: In a medical context, what does 'swelling' mean?
N.explain: 'Swelling' means puffiness or enlargement of a body part.

N.q: Patients who have laser surgery:
N.explain: Laser surgery often allows patients to be treated as outpatients, without hospital admission.
options: have less bleeding yet more pain

N.q: Which type of surgery is associated with lower bleeding, scarring, and soreness?
N.explain: Laser surgery typically results in less bleeding, scarring, and soreness compared to traditional surgery.

N.q: Which type of surgery allows for outpatient procedures?
N.explain: Laser surgery can often be performed on an outpatient basis, while traditional surgery usually requires hospitalization.

N.q: Which type of surgery targets the tumor more precisely?
N.explain: Laser surgery can target tumor cells more precisely than traditional surgery.

N.q: Which type of surgery has a longer operation time?
N.explain: Traditional surgery generally has a longer operation time compared to laser surgery.

N.q: Which type of surgery has higher subsequent infections?
N.explain: Traditional surgery is associated with a higher risk of subsequent infections compared to laser surgery.

N.q: Which type of surgery requires extra training for surgeons?
N.explain: Laser surgery requires additional specialized training for surgeons.

N.q: Which type of surgery has higher safety precautions?
N.explain: Laser surgery requires a higher level of safety precautions.

N.q: Which type of surgery requires additional assistance to maintain equipment?
N.explain: Laser surgery often requires additional assistance to maintain the equipment.

N.q: Which type of surgery is more likely to cause damage to normal tissue?
N.explain: Traditional surgery is more likely to cause damage to normal tissue surrounding the tumor.

N.q: What is a key advantage of laser surgery regarding hospital stay?
N.explain: Laser surgery can often be performed as an outpatient procedure, reducing or eliminating hospital stay.
options: It always requires a long hospital stay
It can be done as an outpatient procedure
It is only available in large hospitals

N.q: What is a disadvantage of laser surgery?
N.explain: Laser surgery requires specialized training for surgeons and higher safety precautions.
options: It causes more bleeding than traditional surgery
It requires specialized training and high safety precautions
It takes longer than traditional surgery

N.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of traditional surgery compared to laser surgery?
N.explain: Traditional surgery has a higher risk of subsequent infections compared to laser surgery.

N.q: Surgery is a medical specialty that uses which techniques?
N.explain: Surgery uses manual and instrumental techniques to diagnose or treat pathological conditions. Using only manual or only instrumental techniques is incomplete, and diagnostic techniques alone are too narrow.

N.q: Surgery uses manual and instrumental techniques to...
N.explain: The primary purpose is to diagnose or treat pathological conditions. Enhancing appearance is only one possible goal of plastic surgery, and closing wounds is only one aspect of surgical care.

N.q: A procedure is considered surgical when it involves...
N.explain: The general rule defines a procedure as surgical when it involves cutting tissues or closing a previous wound. Emergency, plastic, and diagnostic categories are specific types rather than the general rule.
options: Cutting tissues or closure of a previous wound

N.q: Which set lists criteria used to categorize surgical procedures?
N.explain: Surgical procedures are categorized by urgency, type of procedure, body system involved, degree of invasiveness, and special instrumentation. The other sets include factors that are not part of this categorization.
options: Urgency, type of procedure, body system involved, degree of invasiveness, special instrumentation
Urgency, cost, hospital size, surgeon's age, anesthesia
Diagnosis, therapy, cure, appearance, emergency only

N.q: Emergency surgery is intended to prevent...
N.explain: Emergency surgery aims to prevent death, serious disabilities, and loss of limbs and functions. Infection, pain, and scarring may be concerns but are not the defining purpose given.
options: Death or serious disabilities, or loss of limbs and functions

N.q: Exploratory surgery is performed to...
N.explain: Exploratory surgery is diagnostic in purpose: it establishes or aids a diagnosis. Permanently removing pathology is curative, enhancing appearance is plastic, and preventing limb loss is a goal of emergency surgery.

N.q: Plastic surgery is performed to...
N.explain: Plastic surgery enhances the function or appearance of a body part. Permanently removing pathology is curative, establishing diagnosis is exploratory, and preventing death is emergency surgery.
options: Enhance function or appearance of a body part

N.q: Which type is a subtype of therapeutic surgery?
N.explain: Curative surgery is described as a therapeutic procedure, so it is a subtype of therapeutic surgery. Exploratory surgery is diagnostic, and emergency surgery is categorized by urgency.

N.q: Which statement is correct about curative and therapeutic surgery?
N.explain: Curative surgery is a therapeutic procedure, but therapeutic surgery also includes procedures that do not permanently remove a pathology. Therefore, curative is a narrower category than therapeutic.
options: Curative is therapeutic, but not all therapeutic surgery is curative.
Therapeutic is a subtype of curative.

N.q: Which is the best synonym for enhance as used in cosmetic surgery?
N.explain: Enhance means to improve. Remove, diagnose, and delay do not match the meaning of enhancing function or appearance.

N.q: True or False: Surgical procedures are mainly done for therapeutic purposes.
N.explain: The categories include emergency, exploratory, therapeutic, curative, and plastic surgery. Therapeutic is one category, but surgical procedures are not described as mainly therapeutic.

N.q: True or False: Surgeries are mainly carried out by using instrumental methods.
N.explain: Surgery uses manual and instrumental techniques together. It is not described as mainly instrumental.

N.q: True or False: Surgeries are invasive in nature.
N.explain: Surgery involves cutting tissues or closing a previous wound, and degree of invasiveness is a categorization criterion. Therefore, surgery is invasive in nature.

N.q: A patient has a known diagnosis of appendicitis. Surgery is performed to permanently remove the appendix. Which term best fits?
N.explain: The surgery treats a diagnosed condition and permanently removes a pathology, so it is curative. It may also be urgent, but curative is the best fit for permanently removing the appendix.

N.q: A surgeon performs an operation to locate the cause of unexplained abdominal pain. This is best described as
N.explain: Exploratory surgery is performed to establish or aid a diagnosis. The purpose here is to find the cause, not to treat a known condition or remove a pathology.

N.q: A patient is bleeding severely after trauma. Surgery must be done immediately to prevent death. This is...
N.explain: Emergency surgery must be done without delay to prevent death or serious disabilities. The scenario describes immediate intervention for severe trauma.
options: Therapeutic surgery for a previously diagnosed condition

N.q: A patient with a known condition undergoes surgery to treat it. The surgeon removes the pathology permanently. Which labels apply?
N.explain: The surgery treats a previously diagnosed condition, so it is therapeutic. It also permanently removes a pathology, so it is curative.

N.q: Which statement is false?
N.explain: Emergency surgery is defined by urgency and prevention of death, disability, or loss of limbs and functions. It is not always curative.
options: Curative surgery is a therapeutic procedure.
Therapeutic surgery treats a previously diagnosed condition.

N.q: A procedure that only closes a previous wound, without cutting new tissue, is...
N.explain: The general rule includes the closure of a previous wound as a surgical procedure. It does not require cutting new tissue in every case.
options: Still considered surgical by the general rule

N.q: Surgeons need ______ to make ______ during operations.
N.explain: The scalpel makes the incision, the surgical cut. Bandages cover wounds afterwards and do not cut.

N.q: Therapeutic surgery is performed to:
N.explain: Therapeutic means treating, so this surgery acts on a known condition. Diagnostic surgery would only investigate, and cosmetic surgery alters appearance.

N.q: Curative surgery aims to:
N.explain: Curative surgery intends a cure, for example removing a tumor entirely. Palliative care only relieves symptoms without curing.
options: Remove the disease completely and cure the patient

N.q: Emergency surgery is performed:
N.explain: Emergency operations cannot wait because delay threatens life or limb. Elective operations can be scheduled at convenience.
options: At a date chosen by the patient
Immediately, to prevent death or serious harm

N.q: Plastic surgery is also known as:
N.explain: Plastic surgery restores or alters body appearance and function, and cosmetic is its common synonym. It is not defined by urgency or diagnosis.

N.q: To prescribe means:
N.explain: Doctors prescribe by writing the order, while nurses administer by giving the drug. The prescription is the written authorization itself.
options: To physically hand the injection to the patient
To authorize a medicine or treatment for a patient in writing

N.q: Compared with traditional surgery, laser surgery usually causes:
N.explain: The laser seals as it cuts, reducing bleeding, scarring, and soreness. Traditional scalpel cuts heal with more scarring and blood loss.
options: Less bleeding, less scarring, and less soreness

N.q: Which type of surgery is more often done on an outpatient basis, letting the patient go home the same day?
N.explain: Because it is less invasive, laser surgery frequently avoids overnight stays. Traditional open surgery usually needs longer hospitalization.

N.q: What does laser surgery require from the surgical team?
N.explain: The intense beam can damage tissue and eyes, so teams need special training and precautions. It is not safer to operate without preparation.
options: Specialized training and strict safety precautions with the beam

N.q: One limitation of laser surgery is that:
N.explain: Despite its advantages, laser surgery has limitations of cost, availability, and suitability, so traditional methods remain necessary. It does not bleed more by nature.
options: It is not suitable for every operation and needs expensive equipment and training
It cannot be used on skin

N.q: Why is the laser beam described as precise?
N.explain: Precision means exact targeting, and the narrow beam spares healthy tissue around the target. Wide or indiscriminate cutting would be imprecise.
options: It cuts everything in the room
It can target a very small area without cutting surrounding tissue

N.q: Which word is the correct negative-prefix opposite of balance?
N.explain: The standard negative form is imbalance, meaning lack of even distribution or stability. The other formations are not accepted English words.

N.q: The prefix un- in unhygienic means:
N.explain: Un- negates the adjective, so unhygienic means not hygienic or not clean. It is a simple negative prefix.

N.q: In writer and reader, the suffix -er marks:

N.q: Adding -al to biology gives biological, which is:

An adjective meaning relating to biology

N.q: From the verb consult, which noun names the meeting and which names the senior specialist doctor?
N.explain: Consultation is the meeting or session, while consultant names the person, in medicine a senior specialist. The two suffixes -ation and -ant create different meanings.
options: Consultant for the meeting and consultation for the doctor
Consultation for the meeting and consultant for the senior specialist doctor
Consultment for the meeting and consulter for the doctor

N.q: How is the plural of the noun diagnosis formed?

options: By replacing the ending -is with -es to give diagnoses

N.q: Adding -tic to the root of diagnose produces diagnostic, which functions as:
N.explain: Diagnostic is the adjective, as in diagnostic tests used to identify disease. The verb is diagnose and the noun is diagnosis.

N.q: The verb immunize is related to which pair of nouns?

O.q: What is 'insomnia'?
O.explain: Insomnia is the world's most common sleep disorder. Its core feature is a self-perpetuating cycle: stress about not sleeping leads to hyperarousal, which prevents sleep, which then increases stress about sleep. This cycle distinguishes insomnia from occasional restless nights caused by temporary stressors.
options: A rare sleep disorder affecting less than 1% of the population
The world's most common sleep disorder, characterized by a self-perpetuating cycle in which stress about sleeplessness itself prevents sleep
A type of respiratory disorder that occurs only during sleep
A genetic condition present from birth

O.q: What is the core cycle of insomnia?
O.explain: The core cycle of insomnia is self-perpetuating: the very thing keeping you awake is stress about losing sleep. This stress triggers hyperarousal, which makes sleep impossible, which in turn increases stress about sleep. Breaking this cycle is the primary goal of insomnia treatment.
options: Stress about work causes sleeplessness, which then causes work problems
Stress about sleeplessness itself prevents sleep, creating a self-perpetuating loop
Excitement about a trip causes sleeplessness, which then causes fatigue
Physical pain causes sleeplessness, which then increases pain sensitivity

O.q: Which of the following can cause an occasional restless night?
O.explain: Almost anything can cause an occasional restless night, including a snoring partner, physical pain, or emotional distress. These causes are typically temporary and resolve quickly, unlike the chronic self-perpetuating cycle of insomnia.
options: A snoring partner, physical pain, or emotional distress

O.q: How does jet lag affect sleep?
O.explain: Jet lag is a form of extreme sleep deprivation that disrupts the biological clock (circadian rhythm), wreaking havoc on the sleep schedule. It occurs when travel across time zones desynchronizes the internal clock from the external environment. The disruption is usually temporary but can be severe.
options: It has no effect on sleep quality
It disrupts the circadian rhythm, causing sleep deprivation and throwing the sleep schedule out of sync
It only affects people who already have insomnia
It improves sleep quality by resetting the circadian rhythm

O.q: Which long-term conditions can overpower fatigue and cause chronic sleep deprivation?
O.explain: Chronic conditions such as respiratory disorders and gastrointestinal problems can overpower fatigue, preventing the body from achieving restorative rest even when exhaustion is severe. These conditions continuously disrupt sleep architecture and sleep continuity.

O.q: What does the term 'bedroom associations' refer to in the context of insomnia?
O.explain: As sleepless nights accumulate, the bedroom becomes associated with anxiety and wakefulness rather than relaxation and sleep. This conditioned association is a maintaining factor in chronic insomnia. Treatment often involves breaking this association by using the bed only for sleep and leaving the room when unable to sleep.
options: The furniture and decorations in the bedroom
The conditioned mental and emotional link between the bedroom environment and anxiety, restlessness, and sleeplessness
The association between bedroom temperature and sleep quality
The relationship between bed partners and sleep patterns

O.q: What are the 'fight-or-flight' chemicals released during the stress response?
O.explain: During the stress response, the body releases fight-or-flight chemicals, including cortisol and adrenaline (epinephrine). These hormones increase heart rate and blood pressure and jolt the body into hyperarousal. In insomniacs, this response is hijacked at bedtime, preventing sleep.
options: Chemicals that promote deep sleep and relaxation
Cortisol and adrenaline (epinephrine), which prepare the body for danger by increasing heart rate and blood pressure
Chemicals that aid digestion and metabolism
Chemicals that improve mood and reduce anxiety

O.q: What is 'cortisol'?
O.explain: Cortisol is a steroid hormone produced by the adrenal cortex. It is often called the 'stress hormone' because it is released in response to stress and low blood glucose. During the stress response, cortisol increases heart rate, blood pressure, and glucose availability. In insomnia, elevated nighttime cortisol contributes to hyperarousal.
options: A sleep-promoting hormone produced by the pineal gland
A primary stress hormone produced by the adrenal glands that increases heart rate and blood pressure during the stress response
A digestive enzyme that breaks down carbohydrates

O.q: What is 'hyperarousal' in the context of insomnia?
O.explain: Hyperarousal is a condition where cortisol and ACTH jolt the body into heightened alertness. The brain is hunting for potential threats, making it impossible to ignore any slight discomfort or nighttime noise. This state is incompatible with sleep and is a core feature of insomnia.
options: A state of deep, restorative sleep
A state of increased physiological and psychological arousal, where the brain is hypersensitive to potential threats or discomfort
A state of confusion and disorientation upon waking
A state of relaxation and calmness

O.q: What is the brain's primary source of energy?
O.explain: The brain's primary energy source is cerebral glucose. In healthy sleep, metabolism slows to conserve glucose for waking hours. However, in insomniacs, adrenaline speeds up metabolism during sleep, depleting cerebral glucose stores and causing waking exhaustion.

O.q: What happens to metabolism during healthy sleep?
O.explain: During healthy sleep, metabolism slows to conserve cerebral glucose for waking hours. This energy conservation supports restorative sleep. In contrast, insomniacs experience accelerated metabolism during sleep due to elevated adrenaline, which depletes glucose and prevents rest.
options: It speeds up to burn more glucose for energy
It slows down to conserve glucose for waking hours
It stops completely to allow the brain to rest
It remains unchanged from waking metabolism

O.q: What do PET studies show about the metabolism of insomniacs during sleep?
O.explain: PET (Positron Emission Tomography) studies show that the adrenaline preventing sleep in insomniacs also accelerates their metabolism. During sleep, their bodies work overtime, consuming cerebral glucose at an elevated rate. This metabolic overactivity contributes to waking exhaustion and confusion.
options: Their metabolism slows down more than in healthy sleepers
The adrenaline that prevents sleep also speeds up their metabolisms, depleting cerebral glucose stores
Their brains use less glucose than healthy sleepers
They have no adrenaline production during sleep

O.q: What state do insomniacs typically wake in after a night of poor sleep?
O.explain: Because metabolism works overtime during sleep and restorative rest is not achieved, insomniacs wake in a state of exhaustion, confusion, and stress. This state then restarts the cycle of stress and sleeplessness, perpetuating the insomnia.

O.q: According to standard diagnostic guidelines (such as DSM-5), insomnia is classified as chronic when sleep difficulties occur at least ______ per week for a duration of at least ______.
O.explain:
According to major clinical diagnostic manuals, insomnia is formally classified as chronic when it satisfies the "3x3 rule".
This rule is established by the primary medical reference standards:
DSM-5: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (published by the American Psychiatric Association).
ICSD-3: International Classification of Sleep Disorders, Third Edition (published by the American Academy of Sleep Medicine).

O.q: What is the relationship between insomnia, depression, and anxiety?
O.explain: The chemical mechanisms of insomnia are similar to anxiety attacks found in those with depression and anxiety. Therefore, suffering from any one condition increases the risk of experiencing the other two. This bidirectional relationship means treating one condition can improve the others.
options: Their chemical mechanisms are similar, and suffering from any one increases the risk of experiencing the other two
Insomnia causes depression but not anxiety
Depression causes insomnia but not anxiety

O.q: What is one of the best-understood treatments for insomnia?
O.explain: Managing the stress that leads to hyperarousal is a first-line treatment for insomnia. This approach targets the underlying mechanism—the stress response that floods the body with cortisol and adrenaline—rather than just treating the symptom of sleeplessness.
options: Managing the stress that leads to hyperarousal

O.q: What bedroom environment is recommended to minimize 'threats' during hyperarousal?
O.explain: Making the bedroom dark and comfortably cool minimizes sensory stimulation. Since the hyperaroused brain is hunting for threats, reducing light, noise, and extreme temperatures helps prevent further arousal and supports sleep initiation.
options: Bright and warm to promote relaxation
Dark and comfortably cool to reduce sensory stimulation and minimize perceived threats
Noisy and cluttered to distract the mind
Bright and cold to keep the body alert

O.q: What should you do if you are restless and unable to sleep?
O.explain: If restless, leave the room and wind down with relaxing activities like reading, meditating, or journaling. This prevents the bedroom from becoming associated with anxiety and wakefulness. It also breaks the cycle of lying in bed trying to force sleep, which increases arousal.
options: Stay in bed and try harder to sleep
Leave the room and wind down with relaxing activities like reading, meditating, or journaling
Turn on bright lights and watch television

O.q: How can you regulate your metabolism to help orient your body's biological clock?
O.explain: Setting consistent resting and waking times helps orient the body's biological clock (circadian rhythm). A consistent sleep-wake schedule stabilizes the circadian rhythm, which regulates metabolism, hormone release, and body temperature—all of which influence sleep quality.
options: By setting consistent resting and waking times
By exercising at night before bed
By taking sleeping pills at the same time every night

O.q: What is the 'circadian rhythm'?
O.explain: The circadian rhythm is the body's internal biological clock. It regulates sleep-wake cycles, hormone release, body temperature, and metabolism over approximately 24 hours. It is sensitive to light, which is why avoiding bright lights at night helps signal that it is time for sleep.
options: A type of hormone that regulates sleep
The body's internal biological clock that regulates sleep-wake cycles, hormone release, body temperature, and metabolism over a roughly 24-hour period
A sleep disorder characterized by difficulty falling asleep
A digestive process that occurs during sleep

O.q: What is recommended regarding light exposure at night?
O.explain: The circadian rhythm is sensitive to light. Avoiding bright lights at night helps signal to the body that it is time for sleep. Light exposure, especially blue light, suppresses melatonin production and signals to the brain that it is daytime, making sleep onset more difficult.
options: Avoid bright lights at night to help signal to the body that it's time for sleep
Use bright lights to stay awake longer
Light exposure has no effect on sleep
Only use blue lights at night

O.q: What is the risk associated with over-the-counter sleeping pills?
O.explain: Over-the-counter sleeping pills can be highly addictive, and withdrawal can worsen symptoms. Additionally, there are no reliable medications that help in all cases of insomnia. This is why non-pharmacological approaches, such as stress management and sleep hygiene, are preferred first-line treatments.
options: They are completely safe and effective for everyone
They can be highly addictive, and withdrawal can worsen symptoms
They are the first-line treatment for chronic insomnia
They have no side effects and are not habit-forming

O.q: What is 'delayed sleep phase disorder' (DSPD)?
O.explain: Delayed sleep phase disorder (DSPD) is a less common genetic condition. Approximately 8% of patients diagnosed with chronic insomnia actually have DSPD. People with DSPD have a circadian rhythm significantly longer than 24 hours, which puts their sleep-wake cycle out of sync with conventional schedules.
options: A common form of insomnia caused by stress
A less common genetic problem in which the circadian rhythm is significantly longer than 24 hours, putting sleeping habits out of sync with traditional sleeping hours
A type of anxiety disorder that affects sleep
A respiratory disorder that disrupts sleep

O.q: What characterizes the circadian rhythm of people with delayed sleep phase disorder (DSPD)?
O.explain: People with DSPD have a circadian rhythm significantly longer than 24 hours. This means their natural sleep-wake cycle is delayed relative to the external day. They have difficulty falling asleep at conventional bedtimes but can sleep comfortably on their own delayed schedule when given the opportunity.
options: It is significantly shorter than 24 hours
It is significantly longer than 24 hours
It is absent and they have no circadian rhythm

O.q: How does delayed sleep phase disorder (DSPD) differ from insomnia?
O.explain: Unlike insomnia, DSPD is not caused by increased stress or hyperarousal. People with DSPD can sleep comfortably on their own delayed schedule when given the opportunity. This distinction is important because DSPD requires different treatment approaches than insomnia.
options: DSPD is caused by increased stress, while insomnia is not
DSPD is not due to increased stress, and people with DSPD can sleep comfortably on their own delayed schedule
DSPD is more common than insomnia
DSPD has no effect on sleep patterns

O.q: What percentage of patients diagnosed with chronic insomnia actually have delayed sleep phase disorder (DSPD)?
O.explain: Approximately 8% of patients diagnosed with chronic insomnia are actually suffering from delayed sleep phase disorder (DSPD). This statistic highlights the importance of accurate differential diagnosis before initiating treatment for insomnia, as DSPD requires a different therapeutic approach.

O.q: Why is the sleeping and waking cycle important to maintain?
O.explain: The sleeping and waking cycle is a delicate balance vital for physical and mental wellbeing. Disruptions can affect metabolism, hormone regulation, mood, cognitive function, and immune system function. Maintaining a stable routine supports overall health.
options: It is not important and has no effect on health
It is a delicate balance that is vital to maintain for physical and mental wellbeing
It only affects physical health, not mental health
